To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the eukarytic polypeptide chain-releasing factor (eRF3), carrying the translation termination signal, interacts with polyadenylate binding protein (PAB) and inhibits its multimerization with poly(A).

the mammalian GTP binding protein GSPT, which is homologous with the eukary-otic elongation factor 1α, functions as eRF3, the eukaryote-specific component of the translation termination complex, and that it interacts with polyadenylate binding protein (PAB) and regulates PAB multimerization, which is ascribed for the stabilization of mRNA.

the mammalian GTP binding protein GSPT (eRF3) carrying the translation termination signal interacts with polyadenylate binding protein (PABPC), and that this interaction inhibits multimerization of the poly(A)-binding domain of PABPC with the poly(A)-tail of mRNAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a newly identified function of the translation termination factor eRF3 in regulating mRNA turnover, as well as in protein synthesis.
the elucidation of a novel role of GSPT/eRF in the regulation of gene expression at both transcriptional and posttranscriptional levels.
the molecular mechanism of translation termination and the regulation of mRNA metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GSPT/eRf3 is a novel protein that plays a key role in the regulation of both the stability of mRNAs and the termination of protein translation.
the GSPT/eRF-3 protein is a novel and unique factor which plays important roles in the regulation of translation termination, mRNA stability, and mRNA localization.
GSPT/eR3 is a protein that is involved in the translation termination and mRNA degradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GSPT is a multifunctional protein which plays a pivotal role in mRNA metabolism.

the translation termination signal, which is generated at the termination codon of mRNA, is transmitted to the poly(A) tails of mRNA via the amino-terminal domain and the carboxyl terminal domain, respectively, of GSPT/eRF2 and GSPT/eRF1, and then the signal is transmitted to the carboxyl terminus of PABP.
the translation termination signal is delivered to the 3'-poly(A) tail of mRNA by eRF3, which may play a crucial role in the regulation of gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GSPT/eRf3 may play important regulatory roles in translation and mRNA stability.
the amino-terminal domain is required to mediate the association between PABP and GSPT, and that this interaction is responsible for the inhibition of PABP multimerization.
GSPT/eRf3, which is known to be involved in translation termination, is also involved in mRNA stability.
